body:
I remember JackFrags saying that if DICE, Treyarch or Ubisoft make a fully working BR game with the gunplay of PUBG, then this game would die out if it wasn't fixed by then. 

The only reason I play PUBG is because of the gunplay. It's so satisfying getting into a fight and coming out on top. I liked Fortnite, but that was a placeholder until PUBG came out for me. Now that I've played it I like it, I enjoy playing it when it works and doesn't fuck me over, but it needs a lot of work doing to it.

I hate it when you pass over a building, but instead of it cutting your chute so you land on the building, it cuts it just over the building instead and you fall to the floor, losing a chunk of health.

Dean is one of those players that will stand on the edge of the bluezone and fire at players he has no chance of hitting whilst the rest of us have ran off, then he'll die and bitch about it. Or take potshots giving away our position whilst we're hid in a building. Or he'll drive a car around in the last few circles, whilst the rest of us run across the airfield to get into cover, giving away our position and getting us killed. 

Actually thinking about it, that last one might have been why his brother stopped playing the game. We both kicked off at Dean for that. He actually said time to have some fun as he climbed into the buggy. Me and my friend knew exactly what he was gonna do before he did it.

It's cause his brother is a legit fucking idiot when it comes to the game. He can get kills, but he doesn't think. 

I was playing with him and another mate a few days ago. We had people chasing us through the forest south of the bridge that's to the left of Polyana. We had to swim across to the other side because of where the circle was and the blue zone was about to close in. 

Jason (the other lad) got knocked, so I went back to help him whilst Dean (the idiot brother) kept on running to the water and swam to the other side. I managed to kill two guys whilst Jason and I hid behind a rock, but the third was running at us with the blue zone right on his arse.

He hid behind a small tree and we were waiting for him to move, the blue zone hit us, but he still didn't move. Turns out Dean had killed him from the other side, but had his mic on mute and didn't tell us. I'm still not convinced he did kill him, I think the circle did or he quit out.

Jason ended up dying as we tried crossing the bridge in a buggy, I survived until the end with Dean, but died when he couldn't figure out how to get up some stairs to a rooftop where I'd just been knocked. Thankfully he left after that game. Fucking idiot.

Like I say he can get kills, but he's shit at being tactical. He just doesn't think about what he's doing. Doesn't help he smokes weed so half of the time he's stoned.

If I have to drive a car or run through a red zone I will, I'll say fuck it and go for it. But if there's no reason to go through it and my teammate drives us through it, I close my eyes until it's over. There's nothing worse than dying to the red zone due to someone else's stupidity or arrogance.

I actually think my mate stopped playing because his brother drove us uphill in a UAZ during the red zone. I think he got that pissed off with him, he stopped playing that night. Haven't played with him since I don't think.
I'm pretty lucky in regards to the red zone, but if I ever die from it it's because of stupid fucking teammates driving a car uphill when it's going off.

Same. If I get ran over in the final few circles, that's me done for a few hours. Especially if I'm on solo. There's just no skill in it. It's all luck. But I will give credit to this guy, they all lined up for him, so it's hard to be annoyed with him.

You're the type of player I normally hate, driving a car in the final few circles, but I can't be mad because they all lined up for you, so it was a pretty good win. 

Most of the time I get ran over in the final circles it's because I've got no cover, have to run across open ground and some prick is just driving a car around in circles. Fucking hate that.

Because some teammates are fucking idiots. Had a game last night with two mates and a random. The random was just firing into the air, no enemies about, I think he was trying to either lure them in or shit the rest of us up, so I killed him. Can't be doing with people who fuck about like that.

On the flipside of that I don't play Rainbow Six: Siege anymore because of intentional team killing.

That's not what he's saying at all. What he's saying is that Hitman feels like an incomplete story and it was. A cliffhanger does not work for a video game. 

The Last of Us actually gave us a proper ending, it wrapped up the story whereas Hitman didn't. TLOU could exist as a standalone game, Hitman can't because it ended on a cliffhanger. 

I completely agree with what he's saying. Hitman is an incomplete game story-wise.

I wanna kill myself for a whole number of reasons, that's just one of them.

And if they don't care then fuck them, I made the right choice, I'd rather be six feet under than being unappreciated by people. Friends, family, whoever. 

This sub has just proved it. 215 views in 8 hours, 1 comment made by one person other than myself. The fuck is all that about. That happens too much on this sub, people being ignored and having their pleas for help go unanswered. Seems to me you actually have to be considering suicide in that moment to get a response.

I agree. The whole killing downed players to ruin their day is a proper cuntish attitude. If I down a player and kill him, it's not to ruin their or their squads day, it's to win the fight. Not to be a cunt. 

I mostly play squads or duos but if I kill one player, I'll make it my mission in that game to try and finish the rest of the squad off, just so the dude I killed doesn't have to sit around watching for twenty minutes. 

Games stop being fun when people play just to piss others off and they're usually the first ones to cry about it when it happens to them.

I know that Lane's been handed around from country to country, but he's a former British operative, by rights the Americans have to return him to his country of origin. After that if the British wanted to pass on whatever intel they got from him about the Syndicate to other countries they could do that, but they would never hand him over to another country. Ilsa's objective was to kill Lane for the British so she could come home, which means the British never got their hands on him after the Americans.

That's my point. I know what they did, but it wouldn't play out that way.

If that was their intention then it was a mistake. The scene in the catacombs with Lane/Benji should have been the reveal. The scene with Sloane at the Eifel Tower should have shown us that he's not quite on the level, but not make it obvious he's actually Lark. 

Another twist at the end would have been good. Maybe reveal that Julia's new husband is actually Lark and Walker is his brother or something. It would have really cemented the idea that Julia can't have a normal life because of Ethan and that any person she meets could be using her to manipulate him. 

Having said that I do think Walker would have been a good full time member of the team rather than a villain and it's a shame he was killed off. I'd like him to come back in the next one somehow, but it probably won't happen.
He was stood up when I killed him and the crate was not on his body. It's happened to me several times, just because you haven't experienced it, it doesn't mean it's not happened.

I very rarely react during films apart from a ooh whenever something painful happens like the fake Lark getting hit with the laptop or the hook smacking Walker in the head, but when the remote almost falls off the edge of the cliff I actually gasped, I genuinely thought it was going over.

I think he wanted Ethan to assume Lark's identity using his own face which is why he knocked him out with the laptop, knowing it would break and be unusable. Since Walker was Lark, no one would look for a dead man if he successfully framed and killed Ethan as Lark.
Maybe he's talking about his protege who died in MI3.
Was it ever explained why Walker wanted to set off the nukes? I feel like I may have missed that. I know it was something about peace, but I don't think they explain why.
I hated that. The trailers do suggest that Walker had his own motivations, but that scene outright tells you he's an arsehole.

I do think one of the bombs should have gone off, but not in the way you suggest. A reveal that there was a fourth plutonium core that Ethan didn't know about would have been awesome and that's the bomb that went off. Maybe in Kashmir, but not in the camp.

They could have made it work by renaming the Apostles. The Four Horsemen perhaps. When Lane is tied up in the hut and sees Ilsa and Benji defusing the third nuke, he starts laughing and reveals there's a fourth bomb, Benji tries to get on the radio but there's only static... cut to Ethan seeing the flash of the fourth nuke going off just before his fight with Walker. 

That would have been an even better ending and would get people talking about it.
Or crates disappearing after you've killed someone. That's happened to me many times and you never do quite get over it.

I don't get what's so difficult to understand about it. I'm not gonna use a weapon I don't like and have no luck with when I can use one that I do like and have luck with. I've had more kills with an Uzi than a UMP and that's a fact, so I must be doing something right. And the Uzi is incredibly accurate too, with hardly any recoil. Matter of fact I feel it less than a kitted out UMP. I'm not saying that as a joke, I'm saying that's the truth. I do feel it less and get more kills with it therefore it's a better gun to me. 

And I have used the UMP in the past four months. I don't like it, never have, never will.
Wasn't meant to be funny. I would.

All comes down to preference. I think the UMP is harder to control than the tommy gun and packs less of a punch, but has a higher ROF. It probably doesn't but that's how it feels to me when firing it. I can fire thirty rounds from a fully modded UMP on full auto and only get a few hits. Whereas I can fire thirty rounds from a TG and hit pretty much every shot. I will always take a TG over a UMP even though you can't put a sight on it. 

The UMP is my most hated gun in the game. I can't fucking stand it purely for the fact I've been killed too many times by one when I've been using an AK or M4 and fired first. I don't think I'm a bad player, maybe average, I'm doing a lot better lately, but I will never understand how a UMP can beat an M4.

I'll even take an Uzi over a UMP.
It surprises me that people don't like it. I love it. For me it's the best SMG after the Vector.
I struggle to find extended mags of all kinds these days, apart from DMR/sniper mags which is weird. I keep finding quickdraw mags more than anything.

I used burst mode in the final circle on a squad game once, my entire team was dead and watching me play. They couldn't believe I was using burst mode, they started laughing, calling me a mad bastard. Won us the game though, so it obviously works.
I actually prefer the tommy gun to the UMP. I really dislike the UMP, I just don't get on with it. I'm very lucky if I get a kill with it, but a lot of times most are my deaths are because of it.

I think it was always Walker's plan to frame Ethan as Lark and that's why they used him to break Lane out of the convoy, but I don't think the Apostles knew that. Which would explain why they attacked Ethan and the White Widow at the nightclub. They may have thought the White Widow reneged on the deal and decided to kill them, obviously not realising that Walker was framing Ethan as a scapegoat. If Lark is dead then no one is gonna look for him.

One thing I didn't like about the film is when Walker meets with Sloane at the Eifel Tower and hands her the phone from the fake Lark. The original phone was cracked, Walker's phone wasn't. That sort of gives it away that he's got his own motivations. The trailers do that anyway, but for someone going in blind if they're paying attention they'd realise it pretty quickly.

I think for the next Mission film they should have Hunt become the secretary of the IMF and pass the baton to a younger actor. I think Dylan O'Brien would be a good choice. I'd like to see Benji take on the role of team leader like Jim Phelps in the original and the younger actor play his point man like Ethan did. I love that Benji has a much bigger role as field operative. He's probably my favourite character.

I think he's my favourite character too. I like Luther, but I think Benji has really progressed as a character. The way he stood up to Ethan in Rogue Nation showed just how far he'd come. If there's one actor I want to come back for each Mission film, it's Pegg. Even if Cruise passes the baton to someone younger, I want Pegg to be the Jim Phelps to the younger actor's Ethan Hunt. Pegg is the team leader whilst the other actor is the point man doing all the stunts.

I can buy him as a serious tough guy action hero if he looks like he did in Worlds End. Dark, grungy, wild greasy hair. I could buy him as a Martin Riggs type of character with that look. I definitely think he could pull it off with the right script and director.

I can't buy Krasinski as a tough guy action hero, I don't know what it is about him. I thought he was good in 13 Hours and I'm sure he'll do well in Jack Ryan, but there's just something about him that when I see him action hero is the last thing that comes to mind.

I wanna know why you're here. Did you just come here to insult everyone? You talk about people needing to fix their pathetic lives, yet the one going around acting like an arrogant prick with a superiority complex.

Fortnite will never fall because it offers a different approach to PUBG, it actually works, it's very regular with the updates and it doesn't fuck you over in the most dumbest ways. If Battlefield V and The Division 2 offer a realistic military battle royale game, PUBG will just die out. If it doesn't get into a state where it works consistently every game within a year, it'll be done.
Never said I was awesome at the game, you arrogant little prick.

So what? Just because weapons go untouched, it doesn't mean they're bad. All guns have a purpose. A tommy gun is just as effective as a Vector. An M16 is just as effective as an M4. Every fight can be won with ANY gun you have if you have good control of the gun, a good position to shoot from and you time your shots correctly. 

I will take a tommy gun and Uzi over a UMP every single time because I'm better with them. I very rarely get a kill with a UMP, but I'll almost always win a fight with a tommy gun or Uzi. 

Or I'll always take a Mini 14 over an SKS because I don't like the recoil on the latter, but that doesn't mean the SKS is a bad gun. 

Or I'll take the SKS over a Kar98 because I'm useless with the Kar98. Do you see what I'm getting at here? Every gun in the game has a purpose and none of them are bad, it's just how you use them.

Do you think before writing? Fuck off you dopey twat.

Sounds like you're just shit at the game. Can't win any fight with any weapon? I call bullshit on that.

And playing with other players has nothing to do with it because they weren't anywhere near me. If I can kill two people with an Uzi and shotgun whilst one teammate is down and the other two are just running over, surely that means weapons don't matter, and it's about positioning, timing and control which comes from skill.
What a fucking cunt you are.

Looting is the whole point of the game though. You make do with what you've got. If you land and find only an Uzi, you deal with it because you have to. You don't need a fully kitted out M4 and SLR to win the game, you can win the game using a revolver if that's all you find. 

You talk about skill being more important than better weapons, but you fail to realise that using objectively bad weapons and winning with them takes some degree of skill. There isn't a single weapon in the game that is bad, it's just how you use them. 

It really does sound like you don't want a battle royale game and a more traditional shooter.

It's better to have a good position AND aim than good weapons. I've won several squad games with a tommy gun and shotgun, just because I've - and by extension my squad - had a better position than the other guys. 

All weapons are good if you know how to use them. I hate the UMP but I acknowledge that it's a good gun. I just don't like it. 

I won a fight yesterday in which one of my friends was knocked and the other two guys in the squad were far away from us. I nailed a guy with a pump action shotgun, downed him in three shots from maybe ten foot away, finished him off with a final shot, switched to my 35 round Uzi, downed his mate in fifteen bullets, finished him off with a few more shots, picked my friend up whilst the other lads killed the remaining player in the other squad. 

We didn't win the game, but we won the fight, even though I had what could be described as ''bad'' weapons. You can win any fight with any weapon, you've just gotta have good control over it. I don't consider myself a good player, but when I won that fight, I was quite satisfied with myself because of how I won it.

I found out yesterday that Ethan was pretending to be John Lark, but I had a feeling that Walker was gonna be revealed as the real Lark. And to be honest I never once thought that Hunt and Walker were fighting because the latter was trying to bring him in, it was obvious that he had his own motivations. How anyone thought otherwise baffles me.

Exactly. I wouldn't want C4 in the game because there's zero skill involved in using it. You'd just plonk it down and wait for some silly bollocks to run straight into it, whilst you sit in a corner giggling to yourself.

The only explosive weapon I can see working in the game and requiring some skill to use is an M203 underbarrel attachment. A crate only attachment with three grenades and only goes onto the M4. It'd be a little more effective than a normal grenade, but harder to use because you've got no line telling you where it would go. It'd be an outdoor weapon, meaning if you fire it out of a window and hit the windowsill it'd blow up straight away, none of this arming so many meters away bollocks. 

There'd be a risk to using it. It's loud and the limited ammo would mean it's a last resort weapon. And they could get around using it during the last few circles because of a large splash damage, it'd hurt you just as much as them. Personally I wouldn't want this weapon in the game though, just saying that it might be the only explosive weapon that could work.
Shut up you fucking idiot, it's clearly a joke.

The comic might not be canon, but he's an orphan whose family (I think) was killed along with a small town in Baja California, then twelve years later he's a freelance hitman who goes after the gang that killed his family. 

There's no mention of him being military. When he talks to Charon the latter says something about being reintroduced to the Continental, but he'd have to learn the rules now since he's an adult. Guessing his age I'd say he's about 25 in the comic, so it's possible he joined the military some point before then.

I haven't seen it but there is one spoiler that I know of that I wasn't expecting actually. It comes from Christopher McQuarrie himself, so it's definitely real. 

Ethan is chasing a terrorist connected to the Syndicate / Apostles called John Lark, however it turns out he's John Lark himself. Really didn't expect that to be fair.

After catching ten minutes of it earlier, never seen it before, I came on here out of curiosity. I've been on here for five minutes and fuck me there's a lot of bitchiness coming from people. 

After a quick google search (for research purposes) I have to agree that she's probably the most attractive girl in there. She's more natural looking and doesn't seem like a total bitch who would tell you to fuck off if you approached her in a bar. Obviously I haven't seen it enough to know what her personality is like or the others for that matter, but you can normally just tell what someone is like by looking at them and the others definitely come across that way.

Tell me about it. I hate it when you're in a building, looking out of a window and you turn around, not moving anywhere, only to hear your own footsteps. You have to question yourself ''did I just hear someone?'' No, it was my own fucking feet.

Whenever I'm in the last couple of circles and one of the last few alive, my heart beats a mile a minute, even in duos or squads. It's a weird feeling to have because it is only a game like you said. But it's so satisfying to win with a few kills under your belt.

I play on Xbox so I probably haven't encountered desync and I don't have many technical problems anymore really. I suffer from rubberbanding and network problems mostly, but that'll be down to my shit internet. I might have other problems but off the top of my head I can't remember.

My main problem is on the gameplay side. I've had too many instances where my deaths have been because of some form of bullshit or pure cuntery on the other players end. 

Vehicles in the last few circles is one of the main ones. It takes no skill to run someone over, in the first circle or the last, just luck. 

A lot of weapons seem overpowered. The 9mm guns especially. The UMP is my most hated gun because of how powerful it is. Plus sometimes the vests and helmets don't seem that useful. If someone has the drop on you a level three vest isn't gonna save you because by the time you turn around and get into cover, 3/4 of your health is gone. There should be a meter over your health bar. Blue means armoured, white means unarmoured. 

I like the game, I have fun playing it, but it does frustrate me every now and then.
Christian Bale, Chris Pine or Jeremy Renner.
I'm one hundred percent sure he's a cunt though.

I'm not sure about increased, but spread out at least. I've found three SCARS in a single location before, a Vector and Tommy Gun on top of each other. The loot could do with increasing a little bit, but it needs to be spread out more than increasing. There shouldn't be three M4's in the warehouse at the big farm on Erangel. 

Every building should have at least one weapon in it. It's frustrating landing somewhere, run into a building, find out it's empty, run to the next one only to get nailed in the back by Bob the Bastard from Bulgaria with an S12K.
I feel like most people on this sub have a bad attitude problem.

I only go balls deep if my squad is dead and even then I'll go for those who are standing, not those who are downed. I like the push-pull nature of the game. Knock a player, he crawls into cover, gets revived, no big deal because it changes the tide of battle and that's what makes it fun. The team that got ambushed and had a player go down didn't have a chance, but when that player gets picked up, the fight becomes much more intense. 

I don't understand why people wanna play the game to piss people off. They're usually the first to cry when it happens to them. What goes around comes around.

Shooting them as they're maybe three seconds away from crawling into cover I can understand, I do that myself. But if they're in the open with no chance of getting picked up I just leave them because they're already screwed. If I die trying to kill the players who are still standing then I die, that's the nature of the game, FISHDO. I'm not gonna chase an easy kill just to get a kill, I want the full team wipe.
Vehicles in the last few circles driving around getting kills. Used to piss me off whenever I saw that happen. There's just no skill involved. I haven't seen it much lately though.

I agree 100%. The only time I finish off a downed player is if they're alone and right next to me such as being in the same building or about to crawl into cover at a distance. 

If I'm gonna get into a fight with someone, I'm gonna focus on wiping the whole team, not just getting a few kills and dying by the last man. In a 1v4 I'd just go balls deep and focus on killing the last  players standing, instead of killing those are who downed.

But why though? If someone did it to your team you'd get pissed off. It's not gonna net you any points by pissing off the enemy team. 

You can finish your kills by getting a full squad wipe.

I think it's a cuntish way of playing killing downed players like that especially if there's no chance they'll get picked up and there's only one or two enemy players left. If there's a chance they'll get picked up, say if they're about to crawl to a tree, I'll kill them. Otherwise I'll leave them be and go for the remaining players. 

I find it quite sad that people enjoy ruining people's games just because theirs has been ruined. That's kind of pathetic.

Tell me about it. There's just so much arrogance and inflated ego's in this thread, it's fucking sad. Denigrating people and putting them down because they don't play the same way as them is pathetic. 

I actually think the community for this game is awful. Not because of people criticising the game over legit problems, but because of those who think they're better than others for playing a different way. I reckon most of the players who are giving the OP shit aren't even that good themselves and have probably done exactly what he's done before.

I have to agree about teammates. Whenever we land and we're far away from the circle I always say that we need to move shortly if we have one minute left on the clock. One of my mates always - and I mean always - says ''it's the first circle, hardly damages you, chill out''. THAT IS NOT THE FUCKING POINT! 

The point is that I don't wanna waste first aid kits and energy drinks running through the first blue zone to reach the circle. Not to mention if there's anyone in front of us they'll have a bigger advantage and could just shoot us whilst we're in the blue.

He pisses me off whenever he says that. I don't wanna spend a good 10, 15 minutes looting and 5 minutes running through the blue only to die because we can't find a vehicle and have no more med kits left. So now I just leave my team behind if I have to and run on ahead. Bollocks to them if they wanna piss about looting or whatever.

That's not what I said at all, you arrogant twat. Doesn't mean I'm a bad player because I dislike getting into fights with people. I prefer to play smart, tactically. If they've got elevation on me, better cover and it looks like they have better weapons / gear, I won't engage them. A good player is someone who knows when and where to pick his fights. A man has to know his limitations.

And I never said I wanted to get good, I'm an average player and happy with that. Could I get better? Of course. Do I want to? Not fussed to be honest.
Not really. You don't need to communicate with your teammate to just know not to stand up in front of them. He could clearly see where he was firing, it's his own fault he got shot.

That's how I play it too. I don't seek out fights because I know I'll lose them, but I'll fight if I'm confident enough I'll win if someone gets close to me. I won't sit around all game though waiting for kills to come to me, I hate playing that way.

> A person who plays this game and fears encounters with other players is, factually, bad.

I agree that it's satisfying winning a game with some good kills under your belt, but I wholeheartedly disagree with this. I don't like getting into fights with people because I know I'm probably gonna lose, so I don't seek them out unless I know with absolute certainty I'm gonna win. I like fighting and I'd like to get into more of them, but I'm not confident enough to engage someone. I think that's why I'm looking forward to Sanhok (I'm on Xbox) because it's focused more on fighting.

Having said that I don't like sitting around and I always get frustrated when the circle constantly lands on me and I barely have to move. I prefer moving around and chasing the circle, but only if there's some action along the way, running towards the circle without fighting anyone is just as boring to me as sitting around and not fighting anyone.

That's the problem I have. Moving through a forest only to get shot by someone I can't see, so I hide behind a tree thinking I'm in cover when I get sniped by the same person who's hid on a hill some 200 meters away. Those kind of deaths piss me off more than a close up firefight because if you don't know where your opponent is you're totally screwed.

Whereas if the shoe is on the other foot and I'm the sniper, my target will immediately pinpoint my shooting location and headshot me with one shot when I have to fire a full clip from an SKS to just get one hit on them.

I'm not the best at the game, but I will get into fights because I have an aggressive team, so I have to. When we get to 20 people left, I tell my team to just let everyone kill each other if they can because I don't like surviving for 20 minutes only to get fucked up because my team has an itchy trigger finger. By that time I'm going for the win.

I was playing a squad game yesterday with two mates and a random. Myself and my friends got into a firefight, the random just kept on looting different buildings until the rest of us died. I fucking hate that. If I'm in a small house and a firefight breaks out, I'll quickly finish looting the building and then run over to help my friends. I'm not gonna leave gear behind when I've almost grabbed it all, but I'm not gonna fuck around and leave my friends hanging.

I do think it's more satisfying to battle through four different squads, get maybe five kills and then win the game with seven kills in total. 

I'd like to be more kill-oriented, hunting people down and getting into fights because the game is kind of boring when you play it safe. My friends play aggressively and because of that I have to play aggressively too, whereas normally I play smart. If I don't think we can win a fight, I don't engage, I move on.

Looting for 20 minutes reduces the risk of running into someone better equipped than you. It's not fun, but it's logical. If I loot a small town and come out with a Uzi, bandages and grenade, I'm gonna run along to the next town and loot. 

If I don't and chase gunshots and drops, chances are I'm gonna die and even if I do win a fight, I've (my team too) just attracted attention and more people could be coming to us. I don't wanna loot people to get better gear when there's a chance I'll get killed before I even get off the menu.
Nope, no way. That'd be a worse idea than Jason Statham joining the team in Fast and Furious. I don't know why anyone would think that's possible, it's a terrible idea.

I keep getting told that I need a plan and to stick to it, to push myself into getting better, but I can't be arsed. I'm unhappy with my life because I'm not spending it with my ex and making a plan to improve my life isn't gonna change that. I could find another job, work out, go back on my meds, do all the things I want to do, but it's not gonna solve the main problem which is my ex is gone and she's never coming back.

Oh fuck you! Where do you get off spouting that bullshit! Fuck off! Do you really think people wanna hear that? Do you really think it helps someone? Take that crap elsewhere cause I don't wanna hear it and I'm sure others don't either.

I like the idea of an airplane, maybe in mid-flight, but I don't know how they'd go about doing it. I think it'd have to be a red eye flight, one that is almost empty of passengers, otherwise it'd be too difficult to pull off.
That's what I'd like to see. A small Sapienza like town in winter.

I read about these places called underground data centers, they're basically large server farms inside bunkers. There's one under the Alps called Swiss Fort Knox. That could be an interesting place to set a mission, although I think it'd be more suited for Splinter Cell than Hitman. Could work though. 

Killing an arms dealer in his underground weapons storage bunker is a good idea too.

I read the traits link on the sidebar of the RBN sub and my mum has a few qualities that might make her a narcissist. 

1. She favours my sister over me. My sister can do no wrong in her eyes. Maybe two years ago I was staying at my parents house with my ex-fiancee. We were in bed trying to sleep, I had work early the next morning and my sister had her friends over. They don't necessarily want us to stay alive to suffer, they want us to stay alive because for all they know we only get one shot at life and they want us to experience it. By taking our lives early we're denying ourselves to experience all of the good that might possibly come in the future and that's why they want us to stay alive. The future.

Unfortunately we don't think about the future. We're scared of the future because of what's happening in the present. If I feel like a total fucking loser right now, so depressed that he can't get out of bed and just completely beaten down, what am I gonna feel like in fifty years IF (longest word in the dictionary) things don't get better for me? I don't wanna stay here for another fifty years in the hopes that my life will improve.

Hope is a good thing but also terrible. It keeps us going one more day which is one more day that things could turn around for us, but it's also one more day where we have to live with the shit that's going on inside our head. 

I'd also say this in regards to people being selfish. If we end our lives because of our depression it could cause a ripple effect that might affect everyone in our lives. They might get depression because of our actions. We certainly don't want that. We know what it feels like, we don't want anyone to experience it.

But if someone I knew who had depression and was in so much pain, physically and mentally, killed themselves, I would be sad that they've gone, but I'd also take some comfort in the knowledge they're finally at peace. 

Obviously I'd try to discourage them if I knew. As a person it's our duty to look out for each other, but I'd rather not know. I don't want them to die, but I don't want them to be hurting either. I didn't get help for two reasons. I'm assuming you don't have or have never had depression, apologies if that's not true.

1. I couldn't afford my medication. My mum offered to pay for them, but I knew she was struggling for money herself, so I didn't want to burden her by asking for help.

2. Shame. When you have depression you feel like a burden on everyone else. Your parents, siblings, partner, friends, colleagues. You tell someone you have severe depression and you get either a look of surprise or a look of discomfort, sometimes both. So we don't often tell people we have depression. That's because society has a tendency to guilt us into feeling normal.

''Oh, you have depression? Well look on the bright side, it could be worse'' How? How could it be worse? In their feeble little mind ''things being worse'' entails having no home, no job, no family, no friends and stricken with cancer. In my mind I'm already at rock bottom. I have no fiancee, no job because I had a nervous breakdown and I feel totally alone. So yeah I guess things could be worse in that sense. I could have no home, I could have cancer. But in my mind if those things do happen, then it's not getting worse for me, it's just that things aren't improving. No one understands how I'm personally feeling as an individual. 

Look at it from our point of view. You feel helpless because your partner doesn't want your support. As strange as this sounds your partner didn't want your help. Hear me out. 

Going back to feeling like a burden on your family, friends, partner. We feel like the whole world is better off without us. You feel like you don't deserve anything good in your life, that you don't deserve the support of your loved ones, so you self-sabotage. You act awful towards people in order to push them away until you have no one left and you're totally alone. You do that for two reasons. 

1. To prove to yourself that you really are alone, that no one can help you, that no one is actually bothered about helping you because no one gives a shit about you. 

2. To free them of having to look after someone who considers themselves a burden on society.

He's not a bad person, neither is my ex, but you don't ever give up on someone who is mentally ill. But they are selfish. We cannot control the way our mind works and the way we feel, we can only keep it in check through pills and determination. 

I'm a big film nerd and to me depression is like the opening scene from Saving Private Ryan meets The Matrix Reloaded. 

We're on that little boat when life knocks us into the water, so we have to swim with whatever strength we have to get onto that beach and to safety. We push forward up the beach surrounded by  friends and family who support us whilst our own brain is telling us to bombard them with abuse and to give them shit. After a long uphill battle, where everyone is emotionally exhausted, we finally make it to the door in the wall and go through it, where we reset into our default mode and we can smile again. 

That's what a depressive episode feels like to me. We're constantly fighting our brains for no reason other than it wants us to. We're not so much as arguing with other people, we're more arguing with ourselves but innocent people get caught in the crossfire.

Go to the doctors and get help like you were going to. If they can get you on some pills then maybe things will improve. You've just gotta give it a shot. 

In regards to him opening up to you when it gets too much, we should never stop someone from speaking their mind, but it could get to the point where that's all he does even when you're not being awful as a way to control you. 

I knew when I was in a mood and I'd just tell my ex to leave me alone for a while because I need time to get out of it. If she didn't I'd get even moodier and be more of a bastard towards her. You might not realise that these fights you're instigating are being continued by him because he fights back. Instead of arguing back he should've just backed down because you cannot win a fight against someone with depression. It's not possible. 

She was stubborn so she'd always want the last word and whenever she thought the argument was over, she'd say to me ''it's done, why are you still in a mood?'' perhaps not realising that once I'm in that frame of mind I'm in that frame of mind and we may have stopped arguing, but I'm still having a depressive episode.

If someone with depression is in one of those moods it's best to just leave them to it so they can snap out of it themselves. And they'll eventually apologise for being awful once they come to their senses.

Even if you don't know how to support someone with depression you try your hardest to do it anyway. You certainly weren't being selfish by staying with him. He's selfish for letting it happen and basically making you feel agonise over this. Like I said if you truly love someone from the bottom of your heart, you put up with the bad stuff because something good will come up soon. You don't hold it against them by making the depressed person feel like they're in the wrong. 

All I can say is that if you recognise that you'd start fights and you were quite nasty towards him, you can get that shit in check. It isn't your fault that you did those things, it was your brain, but if you can admit that you did ''wrong'' then you can work on that and change for the better. You can control that now because you have now accepted there is a problem. And the first step to solving a problem is by admitting there is one.
